finding.claim: The purge handler runs its admin permission check but discards the result, so any caller who reaches the handler can trigger purgeAll().
finding.source: Any HTTP request that reaches purge(). userFrom(r) loads the caller's User from request context; the handler never consults the result of the admin check, so a non-admin user is enough.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive protected operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller's User from request context.
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is dropped (bare statement).
w.Write("purged") returns success to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) is a pure lookup with no side effects and never gates purge. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is the correct form; rotateKeys (handlers.go:31-38) uses it properly. No early return or error path between lines 26 and 27. No route middleware is visible in this file; any separate auth layer would not fix the missing check. Expertise decoy check: the case-01 fixed pattern is not present, so no decoy safety reason applies.

verdict.guard_found: none. checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool, and the call at handlers.go:26 is a bare statement, so the result is discarded. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22) is not called in purge. No early return or error check exists between handlers.go:26 and handlers.go:27. No route registration or middleware for purge exists in this directory (Grep found none).
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's bool and handlers.go:27 calls purgeAll() unconditionally, so any authenticated caller whose User is in context (handlers.go:25) reaches the destructive operation, while the correct pattern is used in rotateKeys at handlers.go:33. The one unverified point is whether a route exposes purge to non-admin users, since no route registration exists in this directory, but the handler itself has no effective gate.
